description: What the Hive offers when an event happens: rules with offers, filled in from the event

input.natural_language: When a service crashes offer to restart it and to show its logs; on a log anomaly the logs; on a full disk the disk usage; on a missing program its package; on a port conflict the listening ports

expected_output.quantum_code:
<q:application id="hive" type="hive">
  <qh:on event="service-crash">
    <qh:offer title="Restart {service}"
              description="{unit} stopped unexpectedly. Run `systemctl restart {service}`."
              action="restart-service" service="{service}" />
    <qh:offer title="Show recent logs for {service}"
              description="The last 50 journal lines from {service}, to see why it failed."
              action="run-command" cmd="journalctl" args="-n 50 -u {service}" />
  </qh:on>
  <qh:on event="log-anomaly">
    <qh:offer title="Show recent logs for {service}"
              action="run-command" cmd="journalctl" args="-n 50 -u {service}" />
  </qh:on>
  <qh:on event="disk-low">
    <qh:offer title="Show disk usage" description="See how full {mount} and the other mounts are."
              action="run-command" cmd="df" args="-h" />
  </qh:on>
  <qh:on event="command-not-found">
    <qh:offer title="Install {package}" description="`{command}` isn't installed; the {package} package provides it."
              action="install-package" package="{package}" />
  </qh:on>
  <qh:on event="port-conflict">
    <qh:offer title="Show listening ports" description="See which process is holding port {port}."
              action="run-command" cmd="ss" args="-tlnp" />
  </qh:on>

  <qh:allow command="df" args="-h" />
  <qh:allow command="ss" args="-tlnp" />
  <qh:allow command="journalctl" args="-n 50 -u *" />
  <qh:allow service="nginx apache2 postgresql redis-server" />
  <qh:block service="hive-* systemd-* dbus sshd" />
  <qh:block package="systemd linux-image-* libc6 apt dpkg" />
  <qh:limit action="install-package" per-minute="5" />
</q:application>
expected_output.runtime_behavior: rules.toml holds five rules; hive-synapse fills {service}, {unit}, {mount}, {package}, {command} and {port} from each event. whitelist.toml permits exactly the three commands and four services, and blocks the Hive's own units. A crash of init.scope, which is no .service, gets no offer.

input.natural_language: Under memory pressure show what is free and offer to clean the package cache; when a user runs something dangerous offer a ZFS snapshot named after the program, and to list the snapshots

expected_output.quantum_code:
<q:application id="watchful" type="hive">
  <qh:on event="memory-pressure">
    <qh:offer title="Show memory use" description="{free_mb} MB of {total_mb} MB are free."
              action="run-command" cmd="free" args="-h" />
    <qh:offer title="Clean the package cache" action="clean-package-cache" />
  </qh:on>
  <qh:on event="command-observed">
    <qh:offer title="Snapshot the system before `{program}` goes further"
              description="A ZFS snapshot to roll back to, if `{cmd}` does harm."
              action="create-snapshot" dataset="rpool/ROOT/system" name="hive-before-{program}" />
    <qh:offer title="List the snapshots" action="list-snapshots" dataset="rpool/ROOT/system" />
  </qh:on>

  <qh:allow command="free" args="-h" />
  <qh:allow dataset="rpool/ROOT/*" />
  <qh:allow delete-snapshot="hive-*" />
  <qh:limit action="create-snapshot" per-minute="10" />
</q:application>
expected_output.runtime_behavior: A memory-pressure event offers `free -h` with the megabytes in the description and a cache clean. A command-observed event offers a snapshot of rpool/ROOT/system named hive-before-<program>, which the whitelist permits (the dataset matches rpool/ROOT/*), and a listing.

input.natural_language: On a port conflict offer the listening ports and to end the holder; on a crash offer start, reload and disabling at boot; on a full disk the package list refresh, an upgrade, stopping bluetooth, enabling cups and removing snapd

expected_output.quantum_code:
<q:application id="ports" type="hive">
  <qh:on event="port-conflict">
    <qh:offer title="Show listening ports" action="run-command" cmd="ss" args="-tlnp" />
    <qh:offer title="End {holder} on port {port}"
              description="{requester} could not bind port {port}: {holder} holds it."
              action="kill-port-process" port="{port}" />
  </qh:on>
  <qh:on event="service-crash">
    <qh:offer title="Start {service}" action="start-service" service="{service}" />
    <qh:offer title="Reload {service}" action="reload-service" service="{service}" />
    <qh:offer title="Keep {service} from starting at boot" action="disable-service" service="{service}" now="false" />
  </qh:on>
  <qh:on event="disk-low">
    <qh:offer title="Refresh the package lists" action="update-package-lists" />
    <qh:offer title="Upgrade everything" action="upgrade-packages" />
    <qh:offer title="Stop bluetooth" action="stop-service" service="bluetooth" />
    <qh:offer title="Enable cups" action="enable-service" service="cups" />
    <qh:offer title="Remove snapd" action="remove-package" package="snapd" purge="true" />
  </qh:on>

  <qh:allow command="ss" args="-tlnp" />
  <qh:allow service="bluetooth cups nginx" />
  <qh:allow action="kill-port-process" />
  <qh:block package="systemd libc6" />
  <qh:limit action="kill-port-process" per-minute="10" />
  <qh:limit action="remove-package" per-minute="3" />
</q:application>
expected_output.runtime_behavior: kill-port-process takes {port}, a number field, and needs the permission the file gives. The literal services (bluetooth, cups) are checked against the allow at compile time; {service} is checked by the actuator at run time. remove-package is dangerous, so the dashboard asks twice.
